look_here_first: Native Texas signalgrass candidate with a TIGHT upright cluster of thick, short flowering branches carrying many blunt, plump 2.4–3 mm spikelets. Compare mature spikelet SIZE AND SHAPE, and small lower glume (~one-quarter to one-third of spikelet) with U. texana and U. reptans. The current image shows the tight head and broad blade, NOT glume structure.

best_field_traits: Warm-season signalgrass with several short, often erect or ascending, densely spikeleted flowering branches.
Plump blunt obovoid mature spikelets around 2.4–3 mm, one basal reduced/sterile floret and a fertile upper floret.
Lower glume generally small, about one-quarter to one-third total spikelet length.
Upper glume and sterile lower lemma with visible crossveins under magnification; upper fertile lemma tough and transversely wrinkled.
Soft broad grass blade, as seen in original source photo, but leaf width alone not diagnostic.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full tuft and base (annual/perennial status confirmation)
Full dense flowering head with scale
One 2.4–3 mm ripe spikelet face and edge
Lower glume relative to entire spikelet length
True ligule and collar, visible sheath
crew_field_check: START WITH THREE SIGNALGRASS HEADS: U. fusca has tight rather chunky spikelet clusters; U. reptans forms a much more delicate spreading narrow-branched head; U. texana has larger (~4.5–6 mm) spikelets along alternate ascending branches. These silhouettes HELP, but reliable separation depends on measuring mature spikelets and the proportion of the LOWER GLUME.
Measure actual mature spikelet(s) with a millimeter ruler.
Inspect lemma/glume or true ligule ONLY where detailed pixels or a collected macro are actually available.
Record uncertain grass to genus, don't force the species from one photo.

comparisons.key_distinctions: U. reptans has looser, often spreading almost star-shaped branches and tiny short 2-mm spikelets, with a very small basal clasping glume. U. texana generally has larger ~4.5–6 mm pointed spikelets and more open, long alternating racemes, lower glume usually about two-thirds spikelet length. For native/introduced calls, show several ripe spikelets with scale rather than relying on the head silhouette.
